title: National Catalogue of Statutory Legal & Regulatory Rules for France

sources: Legifrance (Code de commerce, Code civil, Code du travail, Code général des impôts)

rules.title: Share Capital Deposit & Escrow Certificate
rules.description: Deposit of initial cash contributions forming the share capital with an accredited bank, notaire, or the Caisse des Dépôts, generating the deposit certificate required for signing constitutional bylaws. Mandatory for corporate legal entities (sociétés: SAS, SARL, SASU, EURL); not required for sole proprietorships (EI / micro-entreprises).
rules.whyItApplies: Applicable if choosing a corporate legal structure with share capital (SAS, SARL, SASU, EURL). Sole proprietorships (EI / micro-entreprises) have no share capital requirement.

officialSource.title: Share capital deposit for commercial companies
officialSource.articleReference: Code de commerce, Articles L223-7 et L225-3
officialSource.notes: The deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) is required for company registration filing.

rules.evidenceLabel: Share capital deposit certificate issued by an accredited financial institution

rules.title: Drafting & Formal Execution of Constitutional Bylaws (Statuts)
rules.description: Drafting and signing constitutional bylaws defining corporate governance, corporate purpose, registered name, duration, and shareholding split. Mandatory for corporate entities (sociétés: SAS, SARL, SASU, EURL); individual enterprises (EI / micro-entreprises) do not have legal bylaws.
rules.whyItApplies: Mandatory founding document governing the legal, governance, and operational rules of commercial companies (sociétés).

officialSource.title: Drafting articles of association for a company
officialSource.articleReference: Code civil, Article 1835
officialSource.notes: Bylaws must be initialed and signed by all founding shareholders or sole partner.

rules.evidenceLabel: Executed constitutional bylaws signed by all founding shareholders

rules.title: Publication of Incorporation Notice in Legal Gazette (JAL)
rules.description: Publication of a legal notice of incorporation in an authorized legal gazette (JAL) or certified digital press service (SHAL) in the département of the registered office. Mandatory for commercial company incorporations (sociétés); ordinary EI / micro-enterprise registrations do not require a gazette publication.
rules.whyItApplies: Statutory public notice formality required for commercial companies prior to filing the registration dossier.

officialSource.title: Legal notices: publication in an authorized journal
officialSource.articleReference: Code de commerce, Article R210-3
officialSource.notes: The publication certificate (attestation de parution JAL) is required by the INPI Guichet Unique.

rules.evidenceLabel: Publication certificate issued by an authorized Legal Gazette (JAL)

rules.title: Business Registration via INPI Guichet Unique (SIREN & Official Registry Extract)
rules.description: Mandatory business registration filing via the INPI Guichet Unique portal to register in the National Register of Companies (RNE) and Trade Register (RCS if commercial), issuing official SIREN and SIRET numbers, along with the statutory registration extract (Extrait Kbis for commercial companies/traders, Extrait RNE or Avis SIRENE for individual professionals).
rules.whyItApplies: Under French law (PACTE Act), the INPI Guichet Unique is the sole statutory channel for registering any business or company in France.

officialSource.title: Single window portal for business formalities
officialSource.articleReference: Code de commerce, Article L123-33
officialSource.notes: Assigns official SIREN/SIRET numbers and generates the formal registration extract (Kbis for commercial entities, extrait RNE / avis SIRENE for individual enterprises).

rules.evidenceLabel: Official business registration extract (Extrait Kbis, Extrait RNE, or Guichet Unique filing confirmation)

rules.title: Declaration of Beneficial Ownership (RBE Register)
rules.description: Mandatory statutory declaration identifying any individual exercising direct or indirect control over the company (holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights) under anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations. Applies to registered commercial companies (sociétés); sole proprietorships (EI / micro) without separate corporate personality are exempt.
rules.whyItApplies: Statutory obligation for registered commercial and civil companies (sociétés) in France under AML/CFT directives.

officialSource.authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
officialSource.title: Declaration of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
officialSource.articleReference: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-46 et R561-55
officialSource.notes: Submitted concurrently with the company incorporation filing on the Guichet Unique.

rules.evidenceLabel: Beneficial ownership declaration receipt (RBE)

rules.title: Approval & Filing of Annual Financial Accounts (Greffe du Tribunal)
rules.description: Mandatory annual approval of financial statements by shareholders/partners and filing of annual accounts (bilan, compte de résultat, annexe) with the commercial court registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) within 7 months following the close of each fiscal year. Applicable to commercial companies (SAS, SARL, SASU, EURL); individual enterprises (EI / micro-entrepreneurs) are exempt.
rules.whyItApplies: Mandatory recurring corporate obligation for registered commercial companies (sociétés) under French corporate law.

officialSource.authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
officialSource.title: Filing annual accounts for commercial companies
officialSource.articleReference: Code de commerce, Articles L232-21 à L232-23
officialSource.notes: Failure to file annual accounts can incur civil injunctions from the commercial court president and criminal fines under Article L242-8 du Code de commerce.

rules.evidenceLabel: Annual accounts filing certificate issued by the Greffe

rules.title: Trademark Clearance & Brand Protection (INPI Register)
rules.description: Prior availability search on the INPI database to verify that the proposed brand name and trade sign do not infringe existing trademarks, company names, or domain names, followed by optional trademark filing in relevant Nice classes and IP assignment agreements.
rules.whyItApplies: Recommended intellectual property clearance and brand protection for commercial ventures marketing products, software, or services under a distinctive brand name.

officialSource.authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
officialSource.title: Filing a trademark in France
officialSource.articleReference: Code de la propriété intellectuelle, Articles L711-1 et suivants
officialSource.notes: Search the INPI trademark and trade name database prior to commercial launch to prevent infringement actions.

rules.evidenceLabel: INPI trademark filing certificate or IP assignment agreement

rules.title: GDPR Privacy Policy & Data Subject Disclosures
rules.description: Drafting and publication of a comprehensive Privacy Policy detailing data processing purposes, legal bases, third-party recipients, retention periods, and rights of access, rectification, and erasure.
rules.whyItApplies: Your service collects or processes personal data of individuals residing within the European Union.

officialSource.title: GDPR: Getting started with compliance
officialSource.articleReference: Règlement Général sur la Protection des Données (RGPD), Articles 12, 13 et 14
officialSource.notes: Must be easily accessible on all data collection forms and interfaces.

rules.evidenceLabel: Published Privacy Policy URL or formal documentation

rules.title: Cookie Consent Management & User Tracking Compliance
rules.description: Implementation of a Consent Management Platform (CMP) conforming to CNIL guidelines, enabling website visitors to accept or refuse non-essential cookies and analytics trackers with equal ease.
rules.whyItApplies: Your platform deploys web analytics, audience measurement, or tracking cookies requiring prior free and informed consent.

officialSource.title: Cookies and trackers: applicable regulatory standards
officialSource.articleReference: Loi Informatique et Libertés, Article 82 et Lignes directrices CNIL (Délibération 2020-091)
officialSource.notes: Refusal must be as easy as acceptance (a visible 'Refuse All' button is mandatory).

rules.evidenceLabel: Screenshot or configuration link of the active Cookie Consent Banner

rules.title: Maintenance of GDPR Processing Activities Register (Art. 30)
rules.description: Creation and recurring maintenance of an internal register recording categories of personal data processing (customer accounts, billing, support, personnel). Under GDPR Article 30(5), while enterprises with <250 employees have a statutory exemption for purely occasional processing, maintaining a simplified register is strongly recommended by CNIL and becomes mandatory for recurring customer data processing.
rules.whyItApplies: Recommended compliance practice under CNIL guidelines for ventures processing recurring customer, lead, or account data.

officialSource.title: Register of processing activities (Modèle simplifié CNIL)
officialSource.articleReference: Règlement Général sur la Protection des Données (RGPD), Article 30 (paragraphes 1 et 5)
officialSource.notes: CNIL provides an official downloadable simplified register template tailored for SMEs and recurring activities.

rules.evidenceLabel: Completed GDPR Article 30 Processing Register document

rules.title: Mandatory Legal Notices for Website & App (LCEN)
rules.description: Mandatory publication of complete legal notices on the website or mobile app: company name, legal structure, share capital (if applicable), registered address, RCS and EU VAT numbers, publication director name, and hosting provider details.
rules.whyItApplies: Every electronic communication service open to the public in France is legally required to publish statutory legal notices.

officialSource.title: Mandatory legal disclosures on professional websites
officialSource.articleReference: Loi n° 2004-575 pour la confiance dans l'économie numérique (LCEN), Article 6
officialSource.notes: Failing to provide mandatory legal notices can incur fines up to €75,000 for individuals and €375,000 for legal entities.

rules.evidenceLabel: Direct URL link to public Legal Notices (Mentions Légales) page

rules.title: General Terms of Sale (CGV), Retraction & Consumer Mediation
rules.description: Drafting and pre-purchase acceptance of consumer Terms of Sale specifying total price including taxes (TTC), service execution terms, statutory legal warranties, 14-day statutory right of withdrawal information, and mandatory designation of an accredited consumer mediator.
rules.whyItApplies: Your business sells digital services or products directly to consumer retail customers (B2C) in France.

officialSource.title: Distance selling: consumer contract requirements and mediation
officialSource.articleReference: Code de la consommation, Articles L221-18 et suivants, et Articles L612-1 et suivants (Médiation)
officialSource.notes: Mandatory consumer mediation membership details and retraction form must be provided before checkout.

rules.evidenceLabel: Published General Terms of Sale (CGV) with consumer mediation details

rules.title: B2B Commercial Terms of Sale & Payment Terms
rules.description: Drafting commercial terms of sale applicable to B2B business relationships, specifying payment timelines, statutory late payment interest rates, and mandatory €40 fixed recovery indemnity.
rules.whyItApplies: Your offering addresses businesses, self-employed professionals, or corporate entities.

officialSource.title: Commercial terms of sale between professionals
officialSource.articleReference: Code de commerce, Articles L441-1 et L441-10
officialSource.notes: B2B terms must be communicated upon request to any professional buyer.

rules.evidenceLabel: Formalized B2B Terms of Sale document

rules.title: 3-Click Online Subscription Cancellation Mechanism
rules.description: Integration of a direct, easily accessible, and free online feature allowing consumers to cancel ongoing subscriptions in a simplified workflow not exceeding three clicks.
rules.whyItApplies: You offer recurring subscription plans online to consumer customers in France.

officialSource.title: Electronic contract cancellation in 3 clicks
officialSource.articleReference: Code de la consommation, Article L215-1-1 (Décret n° 2023-417)
officialSource.notes: Mandatory French consumer protection requirement in force since June 1, 2023.

rules.evidenceLabel: Functional verification or screenshot of the 3-click cancellation flow

rules.title: Online Payment Provider Integration & Security (DSP2 & PCI-DSS SAQ-A)
rules.description: Integration of an authorized Payment Service Provider (PSP e.g. Stripe, Adyen, Mollie) supporting Strong Customer Authentication (3DS2) under DSP2 rules, ensuring the merchant operates within PCI-DSS SAQ-A scope without storing or handling raw cardholder data.
rules.whyItApplies: Your platform collects online customer payments, requiring integration with an authorized payment service provider and compliance with merchant data security standards.

officialSource.authority: Banque de France / ACPR / PCI Security Standards Council
officialSource.title: Online payment security standards and merchant PSP delegation
officialSource.articleReference: Code monétaire et financier, Article L133-44 (Directive DSP2) & Norme PCI-DSS (SAQ-A)
officialSource.notes: As an online merchant, you delegate transaction processing and 3DS2 authentication to an authorized PSP. Direct handling of credit card data by non-PSP entities is prohibited under PCI-DSS.

rules.evidenceLabel: Payment gateway configuration receipt or merchant agreement with licensed PSP

rules.title: Marketplace Platform Transparency & Disclosure Rules
rules.description: Drafting platform Terms of Service (CGU) disclosing listing criteria, ranking algorithms, search visibility, vendor status (professional or private individual), and any corporate ownership ties.
rules.whyItApplies: Your venture operates as a digital marketplace connecting buyers and sellers of products or services.

officialSource.title: Online platforms and transparency obligations
officialSource.articleReference: Code de la consommation, Article L111-7 et Décret n° 2017-1434
officialSource.notes: Strict transparency obligations for digital intermediaries and matching platforms.

rules.evidenceLabel: Published Marketplace Terms of Service (CGU)

rules.title: Professional Liability Insurance Coverage (RC Pro)
rules.description: Underwriting a professional civil liability insurance policy (RC Pro) tailored to your business sector. While statutorily mandatory only for regulated professions (health, law, construction, financial intermediation, travel, real estate), it is strongly recommended as an operational safeguard for all commercial and digital ventures to cover client disputes and contractual damages.
rules.whyItApplies: Advisory risk-management guidance for commercial ventures to cover operational liabilities and satisfy client contract terms.

officialSource.title: Professional liability insurance for commercial activities
officialSource.articleReference: Code des assurances, Article L111-1 ; Code civil, Articles 1231-1 et 1240
officialSource.notes: Mandatory for regulated activities under specific sector codes; highly recommended for non-regulated commercial enterprises to satisfy B2B client contract requirements.

rules.evidenceLabel: Valid Professional Liability Insurance (RC Pro) certificate or policy schedule

rules.title: Social Security Affiliation & Founder Social Regime (URSSAF)
rules.description: Registration with the relevant French social security regime for company officers and founders: General Social Security (Régime Général des assimilés-salariés) for SAS/SASU presidents or Self-Employed regime (Sécurité Sociale des Indépendants - SSI) for SARL majority managers and micro-entrepreneurs.
rules.whyItApplies: Statutory obligation for all active business creators and corporate officers in France to affiliate with the competent social security scheme.

officialSource.title: Business creator: social declarations and contributions
officialSource.articleReference: Code de la sécurité sociale, Articles L311-3 et L611-1
officialSource.notes: Initial founder social registration details are automatically transmitted via the INPI Guichet Unique.

rules.evidenceLabel: URSSAF social security affiliation or compliance certificate

rules.title: Pre-Hiring Declarations & Employment Formalities (DPAE / URSSAF)
rules.description: Mandatory transmission of the Prior Declaration of Employment (Déclaration Préalable à l'Embauche - DPAE) to URSSAF before any employee begins work, establishment of the single personnel register (Registre Unique du Personnel), and affiliation with an occupational health service.
rules.whyItApplies: Your business models payroll, salaried employees, or planned personnel hiring, triggering mandatory pre-hiring social declarations.

officialSource.title: Hiring an employee: mandatory formalities (DPAE)
officialSource.articleReference: Code du travail, Articles L1221-10 et R1221-1 et suivants
officialSource.notes: DPAE must be transmitted to URSSAF at the earliest 8 days before hiring and strictly before the effective start of employment.

rules.evidenceLabel: DPAE filing confirmation receipt issued by URSSAF

rules.title: Regulated Activity Licensing & Qualification Checks
rules.description: Verification and acquisition of professional licenses, state certifications, administrative permits, or professional body registrations prior to incorporation if the venture operates in a regulated French sector.
rules.whyItApplies: Your sector exhibits characteristics of regulated professions requiring statutory qualification confirmation.

officialSource.title: Regulated activities in France
officialSource.articleReference: Code de commerce, Article L123-11-1
officialSource.notes: For regulated activities, the commercial court registry rejects incorporation without required permits.

rules.evidenceLabel: State qualification certificate, professional card, or administrative permit

rules.title: Electronic Invoicing & E-Reporting Compliance (Reform 2026/2027)
rules.description: Compliance with the French electronic invoicing and e-reporting reform (loi de finances). (1) Reception Readiness (1 Sept 2026): All VAT-subject entities established in France (including micro-enterprises under franchise en base) must be capable of receiving electronic invoices via an accredited Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP / plateforme agréée) or the public billing portal. (2) Issuance & E-Reporting (1 Sept 2027 for SMEs/micro): Mandatory issuance of structured electronic invoices for domestic B2B sales and transmission of e-reporting transaction/payment data for B2C and international operations.
rules.whyItApplies: Universal statutory reform for all economic entities established in France: reception capability is mandatory from 1 September 2026, followed by phased issuance and e-reporting obligations from 1 September 2027 for SMEs.

officialSource.authority: DGFiP / Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances
officialSource.title: Electronic invoicing and transaction reporting (e-invoicing / e-reporting)
officialSource.articleReference: Code général des impôts, Articles 289 bis, 290 et 290 A ; Décret n° 2024-266
officialSource.notes: Statutory rollout: 1 September 2026 (mandatory reception for all businesses, mandatory issuance for large/ETI); 1 September 2027 (mandatory issuance and e-reporting for SMEs and micro-enterprises). Supported via accredited partner platforms (PDP) and the public portal.

rules.evidenceLabel: PDP account confirmation receipt or electronic invoicing reception setup verification
